text: Hours after submission, the real results come back from ibm_brisbane -- and they look nothing like the simulator's.
On the ideal simulator, the true optimum dominated every run at roughly sixty percent. On real hardware, the top result never clears nine percent.
Worse, in two of three runs, the hardware's single most common answer doesn't even select the right number of assets -- something that never happened once in simulation.
Soren Lindqvist, Felix Nakamura, and Helena Vasquez review the numbers together, confused and a little deflated, with no explanation yet.
The real results are documented precisely. Why they look this way is still an open question.
